swept: A node scan of all 25 wines, every sale and every staged description, for the engine's words() and sentences() (sale two sentences, 15 to 45 words; description 104 to 110), the dish link rule (every printed dish name against the wine's derived firstPickIds, secondFor and offeredWith, and every tier word beside it), the step against the record, BANNED_WORDS, superlatives (best, finest, greatest, most, top, legendary, iconic, world class, every -est word, than any, than anyone), hedges, prices, questions, allergens, dashes, American spellings from the engine's own list, provenance, living names (the engine's list, printed names exempt), every proper name and year against the hay and the house, the eight word run against the s20 and the opening on the printed name. Found: one superlative in effect (Clos des Mouches, the Drouhin house owns more of the clos than anyone), fixed; the other hits were plain facts (decanted only for sediment, only old vines), left as they stand. No dish without a link, no wrong tier, no false step.
